text:
Morgan: FYI — after last night's private deploy patch we have a gap in KMS audit writes for a small subset of hosts. Not a full outage but missing decrypt/audit records in S3 from ~01:12-01:45 UTC. Repro steps and logs below. @oncall please triage.
Eli: How many hosts and which cluster?
Morgan: ~8 hosts in eu-west-1 private cluster (priv-edge). Sam grabbed logs, will paste the critical bits.
Sam: paste:
```
audit-writer[2442]: upload_batch failed: PutObject error: AccessDenied: Access Denied
status code: 403, request id: XXXXXX, host id: yyyy
audit-writer[2442]: fallback: buffering locally to /var/log/audit-buffer/2026-03-20
```
June: Did the KMS client rotation run around that time? We kicked off a rolling rekey + agent restart during the maintenance window.
Carmen: If the uploader role lost kms:Encrypt/GenerateDataKey on the CMK, PutObject to encrypted bucket would fail. Could be RBAC or KMS policy.
Eli: Deploy bot shows a rollout at 01:15 UTC. ops-bot?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout 'priv-edge-rekey-2026-03-20' completed at 01:15 UTC by Eli.
June: Check CloudTrail for GenerateDataKey calls for that CMK. If GenerateDataKey is missing for those hosts, the issue is upstream (agent can't get data key).
Sam: I queried CloudTrail for the CMK — saw GenerateDataKey for most hosts, but the 8 impacted hosts have AccessDenied responses.
Morgan: What changed in RBAC? We recently updated service account bindings for audit-writer to use a new role that includes sts:AssumeRole to the uploader role. Maybe the trust policy got tightened.
Eli: I'm checking the role binding now: `kubectl get rolebinding audit-uploader -n priv-edge -o yaml` shows it references svcacct `audit-writer-sa@priv-edge`. The IAM role mapping was updated in the last commit 4f3a2b.
Carmen: Also verify netpol — audit-writer talks to a local kms-proxy on port 8443. If NetPol was tightened to deny egress for that pod label, the client would fail to contact the proxy and fall back, causing no GenerateDataKey.
Sam: Running quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n priv-edge -l app=audit-writer` then `kubectl exec -n priv-edge audit-writer-... -- curl -v https://kms-proxy:8443/health`
Sam: curl against proxy from an impacted pod returns TLS handshake failure. Non-impacted pods succeed.
June: That smells like netpol or an iptable rule on the node. Did we push any CNI or host-level firewall changes at the same time as the rekey?
Eli: We did push a netpol tighten PR (merge 01:14 UTC) which should only allow 10.0.0.0/16 to kms-proxy. The affected hosts are in a secondary CIDR (10.1.x). Oof.
Morgan: Plan proposal: 1) cordon/taint the 8 impacted nodes to stop new workload placement, 2) reapply netpol to include the secondary CIDR temporarily, 3) restart audit-writer pods to force reattempts, 4) reharvest buffered logs from `/var/log/audit-buffer/` and reingest to S3, 5) rollback role/trust policy change if we see it as contributor. Anyone object?
June: +1. Also add a CloudTrail/CMEK check to the remediation playbook so we don't miss GenerateDataKey AccessDenied traces.
Eli: I'll own the netpol patch and node tainting. Sam will handle pod restarts and reingest. Morgan you own the incident doc and postmortem. Carmen, can you review the IAM trust policy diff?
Carmen: On it — I'll diff 4f3a2b vs previous and post findings here in 10m.
incident-bot: incident-bot: created incident ticket PRIV-AUDIT-GAP-1748801234 (severity: P2).
Morgan: OK starting 15-min triage call in 5 minutes — dropping a zoom link in #eng-ops. Keep replies compact here; we'll capture action owners in the incident ticket.
Eli: quick mitigation note: reapply `priv-edge-netpol-allow-secondary-cidr` as hotfix, then we'll bake a stricter policy with proper CIDR mapping.
Sam: Kicking off reingest once pods are green. Will post progress.
Morgan: Thanks — update the incident ticket with timestamps for reingest and any recovered object lists.
June: After we stabilize, follow-up TODOs: add automated test that simulates serviceaccount->role assume+GenerateDataKey and netpol egress from both CIDRs.
Carmen: forwarded IAM diffs to the ticket and flagged one suspicious trust condition.
Sam: Reingest finished for buffer files up to 01:45 UTC — reingested 6/8 hosts so far, working on last two.
Morgan: Great. We'll keep this thread as the source of truth for notes. If anything changes escalate to P1. Thanks team.
